t: A Deccan dynasty that ruled from Vatapi, modern Badami in northern Karnataka, from about 543 until 753.
Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada and ruled from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal.
Its temples at Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal mark the move from rock-cut caves to free-standing stone temples.
dyk: The Aihole inscription of 634 names the poets Kalidasa and Bharavi, giving one of the earliest firm dates by which Kalidasa’s works were already famous.
ev: Pulakeshin I fortifies the hill of Vatapi and performs a horse sacrifice
Pulakeshin II wins the throne in a civil war against his uncle Mangalesha
Pulakeshin II halts Harsha of Kannauj on the Narmada (date debated)
Conquest of Vengi; Kubja Vishnuvardhana founds the Eastern Chalukyas
Ravikirti composes the Aihole inscription celebrating Pulakeshin II
Pallava king Narasimhavarman I takes Vatapi; Pulakeshin II dies
Vikramaditya II occupies Kanchipuram; Virupaksha temple built at Pattadakal
Dantidurga overthrows Kirtivarman II and founds the Rashtrakuta dynasty
